reader.requirement: At --std 85 the figurative constant ALL literal, where it is not associated with a data item (DISPLAY, which 1985 newly permits it in; the ALPHABET and CLASS literal phrases of SPECIAL-NAMES), must stand for the literal exactly once (its own length), and a figurative constant must be admitted wherever 'literal' appears in a format, subject to the listed exceptions (numeric-restricted positions take only ZERO; multi-character ALL literal with a numeric item is obsolete; ALL before a non-literal figurative is redundant) and to each statement's own bars (STOP, STRING, UNSTRING, INSPECT refuse a figurative beginning with ALL).

edition-consulted.switches: ConstructRegistry.Check(AllLiteralMulticharNumericRemoved2002): a multi-character ALL literal associated with a numeric item is accepted at 1985 (obsolete) and refused COBOL0902 from 2002 (exception 2 of the lead-in)
ConstructRegistry.Check(FigurativeAllZeroNumericRemoved2002): ALL ZERO in a numeric position is accepted at 1985 (ALL redundant, exception 3) and refused from 2002
ConstructRegistry.IsAvailable(StopLiteralRemoved2002): STOP ALL literal refused by §1985:VI.6.24.3 SR1 only where STOP literal exists

reader.edition-search: The length-of-literal rendering itself (OperandText AsStringVisitor.Visit(BoundAllLiteral): the literal once; SpecialNamesBinder.AllLiteralCharacters: literal-1 itself) consults no edition (grep CobolVersion/Edition/ConstructRegistry in OperandText.cs, FigurativeConstants.cs, SpecialNamesBinder.Literals.cs: only EditionContext.Error for diagnostics). The edition is consulted only by the exception gates listed.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: not for the length of an unassociated ALL literal (same at 2023: DISPLAY ALL "AB" prints AB), but the lead-in's exceptions differ: MOVE ALL "12" TO a numeric item runs at 85 (1212) and is refused COBOL0902 at 2023; ALL ZERO as a numeric operand likewise; STOP ALL literal is a 1985-only refusal
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf02_01 covers DISPLAY ALL "AB" / ALL "XYZ"; not the ALPHABET or CLASS literal phrases (the context the 1985 substantive change (1) was written for), the exceptions, or the per-statement ALL bars

reader.notes: An ALL literal binds to BoundAllLiteral; in a string position OperandText renders its literal once, and in an ALPHABET/CLASS literal phrase SpecialNamesBinder takes literal-1 itself, so both unassociated contexts give the literal's own length at 1985, which the probes show. The exceptions of the lead-in are gated per edition through ConstructRegistry rows that keep the 1985 forms legal. INSPECT's refusal of ALL ALL "A" cites §2023:14.9.22.3 SR3 at --std 85 (diagnostic citation only; 1985 INSPECT SR3 says the same).

refuter.evidence: I attacked the lead-in ('A figurative constant may be used whenever literal appears in a format') at literal positions the reader did not probe. al4.cob at --std 85 accepts and runs each one: CLASS IS LOW-VALUE THRU "B" (native-lowest per §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR7, so space is in the class); CLASS IS SPACE QUOTE ZERO; PADDING CHARACTER IS SPACE on a sequential file (OPEN/WRITE/CLOSE ran); 88 VALUE LOW-VALUE THRU "M" / VALUE ALL "AB" / VALUE SPACE (all TRUE as expected); INITIALIZE G REPLACING ALPHANUMERIC BY ALL "AB" NUMERIC BY ZERO gives [ABA00]; COMPUTE N2 = ZERO - 3 gives -03; PERFORM VARYING FROM ZERO gives 03. Exceptions: al6 CURRENCY SIGN IS QUOTE -> COBOL0892 (§1985:VI.4.5.3 SR12). Class c: al5 CALL USING BY CONTENT SPACE (a 2002 literal argument; the 1985 BY CONTENT takes identifier-2 only) -> COBOL0900. Unassociated ALL literal: 1985 has no legal context beyond DISPLAY and the SPECIAL-NAMES literal phrases (the reader probed those). rel1.cob 'IF ALL "AB" = "ABAB"' prints EQ, which extends the ALL literal to the other literal's length, but the program breaks §1985:VI.6.3.1.1 ('must contain at least one reference to a variable'); the compiler warns COBOL3146, already tracked in kb/Work PB5481/PB5826, so this is not conforming source and does not count against GRL2.3. cite.py: OK §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3 GRL2.3 (both the length sentence and the lead-in sentence); OK §1985:VI.4.5.3 SR12; OK §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR7; OK §1985:VI.6.3.1.1.
